whatItMeans: Every processing activity has one documented Art. 6 lawful basis (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests) recorded before any personal data is collected; legitimate-interests basis requires a documented balancing test.
appliesToValueStreams: Technology Delivery & Change; Technology Strategy, Architecture & Delivery

whatItMeans: Health, biometric, genetic and other special-category data (e.g., medical evidence in claims and underwriting) is processed only under an Art. 9(2) condition with heightened safeguards, access controls, and logging.
appliesToValueStreams: Technology Delivery & Change; Cybersecurity, Identity & Resilience

whatItMeans: Where consent is the basis, capture freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous opt-in; store consent records with timestamp and notice version; withdrawal is as easy as granting.
Art. 13/14 information is provided at or before collection in plain, layered language; the served notice version is recorded against the data subject.
Collect only data necessary for the stated purpose; every field has a documented purpose; the design rejects fields without one; no re-use for incompatible purposes.
appliesToValueStreams: Technology Strategy, Architecture & Delivery; Technology Delivery & Change

whatItMeans: Per-data-category retention schedules are enforced; automated deletion or anonymisation occurs at end of retention; no indefinite storage of identifiable data.
appliesToValueStreams: Cybersecurity, Identity & Resilience; Technology Delivery & Change

whatItMeans: Mechanisms keep personal data accurate and allow rectification of inaccurate data without undue delay (within one month of a request).
Data subjects can obtain confirmation of processing and a copy of their data plus processing metadata; fulfilment is machine-assisted and completes within one month.
Verifiable deletion across primary stores, backups, caches, logs, and processors when erasure conditions are met; erasure/rectification is propagated to recipients (Art. 19).
appliesToValueStreams: Technology Delivery & Change; Cybersecurity, Identity & Resilience

whatItMeans: The subject's provided data is exportable in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format (e.g., JSON/CSV); direct transmission to another controller where technically feasible.
Processing-restriction flags and objection (including an absolute opt-out from direct marketing) are enforceable at the data layer and respected by downstream jobs.

For decisions based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects (e.g., automated underwriting, pricing, claims triage), establish a lawful ground, provide meaningful information about the logic, and offer human review and the ability to contest. Crosswalk to the EU AI Act high-risk obligations.
appliesToValueStreams: Technology Strategy, Architecture & Delivery; Technology Delivery & Change

standard: Data Protection by Design & by Default
whatItMeans: Privacy controls (pseudonymisation, minimisation, access limits) are embedded into architecture from inception and the system defaults to the most privacy-protective settings.
A DPIA is completed and signed off before build for high-risk processing; prior consultation with the supervisory authority (Art. 36) occurs where residual risk remains high.
appliesToValueStreams: Technology Strategy, Architecture & Delivery; Technology Delivery & Change

whatItMeans: A living inventory of processing activities, purposes, data categories, recipients, transfers, and retention is maintained and updated as systems change.

Risk-appropriate technical and organisational measures (encryption, pseudonymisation, confidentiality, integrity, availability, resilience, restore capability) are applied and their effectiveness is tested regularly. Links to the Encryption and Application Security standards.
appliesToValueStreams: Cybersecurity, Identity & Resilience; Technology Delivery & Change

whatItMeans: Breaches are detected, assessed, and notified to the supervisory authority within 72 hours where required, and to affected subjects without undue delay where high risk; a breach register is maintained.
Processors and sub-processors are bound by Art. 28 data processing agreements with a documented authorisation chain, audit rights, and instruction-only processing.
Personal data leaves the EEA only under a valid mechanism (adequacy, SCCs, or BCRs) with a transfer impact assessment and supplementary measures where needed (post-Schrems II).
appliesToValueStreams: Technology Strategy, Architecture & Delivery; Cybersecurity, Identity & Resilience

whatItMeans: A DPO is designated, resourced, and independent, and is involved in all personal-data matters; the DPO is the contact point for the authority and data subjects.

Compliance with every privacy control is demonstrable through documented policies, decision records, and audit-ready evidence captured automatically where possible. This is the accountability principle that makes evidence mandatory.
appliesToValueStreams: Cybersecurity, Identity & Resilience; Technology Strategy, Architecture & Delivery
